videos.title: 17 Minutes To Understand Money For The Rest Of Your Life
summary: In this 17-minute episode, Sandeep Swadia lays out his "FREE" framework for building and protecting wealth, arguing that money has two scoreboards: the visible one people flaunt and the invisible one that determines actual life control.

He walks through the framework's four pillars: Freedom (measuring wealth in months of runway rather than dollars), Resilience (recovering from market setbacks), Ego (a three-line pre-investment checklist to curb overconfidence), and Enough (balancing "to-be" and "to-do" priorities so people don't gamble away what they need).
The video is pure personal-finance philosophy with no AI tools, models, or products mentioned; it closes with a parable about a peasant to illustrate the "enough" principle.

videos.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen Just Dropped (Personally Tested)
summary: Paul J Lipsky reviews Google's newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast, cost-efficient model positioned as an everyday "daily driver," after roughly a day of early access.

He covers where Hydrogen is currently available, walks through Google's published benchmarks, and compares its pricing against Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 4 Carbon to place it within Google's current model lineup.
Lipsky then demos several things he built using Hydrogen, offering his take on where the model best fits relative to its faster/cheaper and more capable siblings.

videos.title: Claude can now add features to itself
summary: Futurepedia covers Anthropic's new "Mods" capability, which lets Claude add features directly to its own app based on a user's description of what they want.
The short video frames Mods as a self-extension tool: rather than waiting on Anthropic to ship a feature, users can describe the functionality they want and have Claude build it into the app itself.
Consistent with the channel's quick-hit format, the video is a brief product-update style clip highlighting a single new Claude capability without a lengthy tutorial walkthrough.

videos.title: Claude Makes 3D Animations Easy Now
summary: Futurepedia demonstrates how Claude can now generate polished 3D animations using Three.js, contrasting this approach with the frame-by-frame JavaScript method shown in an earlier motion-graphics video on the channel.

The host walks through building an animation from a single prompt, then introduces a free "3D Style Atlas" of 37 ready-made styles that can be copied directly into Claude, complete with built-in sound effects.
The video closes with a voiceover-mode demo, showing a volcano-themed animation synced to narration, with chapters covering the mechanics, style atlas, and voiceover workflow.
